name: Retail Investor Sentiment
title: Retail Investor Sentiment
answer: Retail investor sentiment is the measurable mood, attention, and directional leaning of non-professional traders toward a security or market theme. It is read from public forums, social media posts, brokerage order flow, options activity, surveys, and news comment sections. The goal is to turn noisy individual expressions into a signal that can be compared with price, volume, and institutional positioning. This section of the atlas treats sentiment as one layer of market language, not as a standalone trading system.

crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

sections.body: Retail investor sentiment is the measurable mood, attention, and directional leaning of non-professional traders toward a security or market theme. It is read from public forums, social media posts, brokerage order flow, options activity, surveys, and news comment sections. The goal is to turn noisy individual expressions into a signal that can be compared with price, volume, and institutional positioning. This section of the atlas treats sentiment as one layer of market language, not as a standalone trading system.
sections.heading: Scope

sections.body: The work runs on scheduled and streaming data pipelines that pull text from platforms such as Reddit, X, StockTwits, and financial news feeds, along with brokerage and exchange data where available. Storage is typically a mix of object stores for raw text, time series databases for aggregated scores, and vector databases for embedding-based retrieval. Compute includes CPU clusters for ingestion and normalization, and GPU instances for transformer models and large language model inference. Access is usually through internal dashboards, notebooks, and APIs that serve daily or intraday sentiment scores.
sections.heading: What it runs on

sections.body: Practitioners collect posts, comments, and headlines, then clean them by removing bots, spam, and duplicate text. They label a sample for positive, negative, or neutral tone, or for themes such as fear, greed, and skepticism. Lexicon-based scoring and fine-tuned transformer classifiers both remain common, with large language models increasingly used to summarize threads and extract stance. The resulting scores are aggregated by ticker, sector, or topic, often weighted by engagement, follower count, or recency, and then compared with returns, volatility, and volume to test whether the sentiment leads or merely echoes price.
sections.heading: How the work is done

sections.body: The main rights issues are platform terms of service, user privacy, and the provenance of scraped or purchased data. Social media sentiment can be gamed through coordinated posts, paid promotion, and fake accounts, so provenance and bot filtering are essential before any score is trusted. Firms must also consider whether using retail sentiment creates a duty of care or a disclosure obligation, especially if the signal is sold or used in client-facing products. No part of this atlas should be read as legal or investment advice, and sentiment data should be treated as observational, not as a recommendation.
sections.heading: Rights, risk and provenance

sections.body: Retail sentiment work is moving toward real-time, ticker-level scoring that blends text with order flow, options skew, and search trends. Multimodal models are beginning to read images, video, and audio from earnings calls and social clips, not just written posts. The next few years will likely bring better bot detection, more standardized sentiment benchmarks, and closer regulatory attention to how retail attention is measured and monetized. The site's tracking of AI-related instruments, lawsuits, and compliance pages will expand as sentiment becomes a more formal part of market surveillance.
